claims: Creator's shipped, paying-customer product had a massive vulnerability that could have cost thousands of dollars

Top 5 vibe-coded vulnerabilities: 1 vulnerable third-party packages, 2 unsafe user inputs (forms), 3 missing permission checks (user impersonation / data access), 4 unprotected databases (esp. Supabase), 5 exposed API keys
Missing permission checks is 'the scariest'; exposed API keys is 'the biggest no-no yet the most common'
AppBully gives a 'how cooked' report, copyable fix prompt or MCP, and monitors the repo on every push
AppBully covers code, database, legal ('we are not a lawyer') and design
how_to_steps: Go to appbully.ai and choose a mode (Baby Gloves / Bully Mode / Savage AF)
AppBully scans and reports findings grouped by Code, Database, Legal, Design
For each finding, copy the fix prompt into Claude Code/Codex, or use the built-in MCP directly
Leave it connected so new pushes are re-scanned
on_screen_only: Overlay 'TOP 5 ISSUES: 1. VULNERABLE PACKAGES 2. UNSAFE USER INPUTS 3. MISSING PERMISSION CHECKS 4. UNPROTECTED DATABASE 5. EXPOSED API KEYS'

relevance.why: The five vulnerability classes are exactly what a solo founder shipping Claude Code apps on Supabase gets wrong; the product pitch is secondary but the checklist is real.

implement_score.why: Immediately: make a Claude Code security-audit skill that checks the five items (npm audit/Dependabot, input validation, per-route auth and RLS on Supabase, secrets in client bundles). Trying AppBully is optional; its MCP approach is worth a look if pricing is sane.
